```{r}

# Import data and convert to log returns
dyn_df <- read_csv('data/indo_us.csv') 



dyn_df$date <- dmy(dyn_df$Date)
dynam <- dyn_df |> mutate(lognifty=log(NIFTY50), logsp500=log(SP500))
# Split data into sub-periods
cut_off_date <- as.Date("2022-02-24")
before_conflict_data <- dynam %>% filter(Date < cut_off_date)
during_conflict_data <- dynam %>% filter(Date >= cut_off_date)

```




```{r}
# Define a function to estimate VAR model and calculate FEVD
estimate_VAR_FEVD <- function(dynam, lag_order) {
  var_model <- VAR(dynam[, c("NIFTY50", "SP500")] %>% na.omit(), p = lag_order)
  fevd_result <- fevd(var_model, n.ahead = 1)
  return(fevd_result)
}

# Estimate VAR and calculate FEVD for both sub-periods
lag_order <- 4  # Adjust as needed
fevd_before_conflict <- estimate_VAR_FEVD(before_conflict_data, lag_order)

fevd_during_conflict <- estimate_VAR_FEVD(during_conflict_data, lag_order)

# Print FEVD results for both sub-periods
print(fevd_before_conflict)
print(fevd_during_conflict)

```




```{r}
# Plot daily returns
ggplot(dynam, aes(x = Date)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = NIFTY50_log, color = "NIFTY50")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = SP500_log, color = "SP500")) +
  labs(title = "Daily Returns of Stock Market Indices",
       y = "Log Returns", color = "Index") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("NIFTY50" = "blue", "SP500" = "red")) +
  theme_minimal()
```




```{r}
# Summary statistics before the crisis
summary_before_conflict <-describe(before_conflict_data) %>% na.omit() %>% 
  select(-vars, -se, -n, -trimmed, -se)

# Create a data frame for the table



table2_data <- summary_before_conflict %>% 
  mutate(
  ADF_Test_Statistic = c(adf_test_before_conflict_NIFTY50$statistic, adf_test_before_conflict_SP500$statistic),
  ADF_Test_P_Value = c(adf_test_before_conflict_NIFTY50$p.value, adf_test_before_conflict_SP500$p.value)
)

# Print table
print(table2_data)

```



```{r}
# Calculate ADF test statistics and p-values for NIFTY50 and SP500
adf_test_before_conflict_NIFTY50 <- adf.test(before_conflict_data$NIFTY50_log)
adf_test_before_conflict_SP500 <- adf.test(before_conflict_data$SP500_log)

# Summary statistics before the crisis
summary_before_conflict <- describe(before_conflict_data) %>% na.omit() %>%
  select(-vars, -se, -n, -trimmed, -mad)  # Exclude unwanted columns

# Create a data frame for Table 2
table2_data <- data.frame(
  Variable = c("NIFTY50", "SP500"),
  Mean = summary_before_conflict$mean,
  StdDev = summary_before_conflict$sd,
  Median = summary_before_conflict$median,
  Min = summary_before_conflict$min,
  Max = summary_before_conflict$max,
  Range = summary_before_conflict$range,
  Skew = summary_before_conflict$skew,
  Kurtosis = summary_before_conflict$kurtosis,
  ADF_Test_Statistic = c(adf_test_before_conflict_NIFTY50$statistic, adf_test_before_conflict_SP500$statistic),
  ADF_Test_P_Value = c(adf_test_before_conflict_NIFTY50$p.value, adf_test_before_conflict_SP500$p.value)
)

# Print table
print(table2_data)

```



```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(vars)
library(tidyverse)

# Import data and convert to log returns
dynam <- read_csv("Dynamics.Analysis.weekly.csv", 
                  col_types = cols(Date = col_date(format = "%d/%m/%Y")))
dynam <- dynam %>%
  arrange(Date) %>%
  mutate(
    NIFTY50_log = log(NIFTY50) - log(lag(NIFTY50)),
    SP500_log = log(SP500) - log(lag(SP500))
  )

# Split data into sub-periods
cut_off_date <- as.Date("2022-02-24")
before_conflict_data <- dynam %>% filter(Date < cut_off_date)
during_conflict_data <- dynam %>% filter(Date >= cut_off_date)

```



```{r}
# Extract spillover effects for NIFTY50 from FEVD
spillover_NIFTY50_before <- fevd_before_conflict$NIFTY50_log$SP500_log

# Create a data frame for the table
table4_data <- data.frame(
  Index = "NIFTY50",
  Spillover_Index = spillover_NIFTY50_before
)

# Print table
print(table4_data)

```



```{r}
# Summary statistics before the crisis
summary_before_conflict <- summary(before_conflict_data[, c("NIFTY50_log", "SP500_log")])
adf_test_before_conflict_NIFTY50 <- adf.test(before_conflict_data$NIFTY50_log)
adf_test_before_conflict_SP500 <- adf.test(before_conflict_data$SP500_log)

# Create a data frame for the table
table2_data <- data.frame(
  Variable = c("NIFTY50", "SP500"),
  Mean = summary_before_conflict[, "mean"],
  StdDev = summary_before_conflict[, "sd"],
  ADF_Test_Statistic = c(adf_test_before_conflict_NIFTY50$statistic, adf_test_before_conflict_SP500$statistic),
  ADF_Test_P_Value = c(adf_test_before_conflict_NIFTY50$p.value, adf_test_before_conflict_SP500$p.value)
)

# Print table
print(table2_data)

```

```{r}
# Calculate conditional volatility
conditional_volatility <- sqrt(rollapply(dynam[, c("NIFTY50_log", "SP500_log")], width = 20, FUN = var))

# Plot daily index volatility
ggplot(dynam, aes(x = Date)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = conditional_volatility$NIFTY50_log, color = "NIFTY50")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = conditional_volatility$SP500_log, color = "SP500")) +
  labs(title = "Daily Index Volatility",
       y = "Volatility", color = "Index") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("NIFTY50" = "blue", "SP500" = "red")) +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}
# Define a function to estimate VAR model and calculate FEVD with varying lag orders
estimate_VAR_FEVD_robust <- function(dynam, lag_order) {
  var_model <- VAR(dynam[, c("lognifty", "logsp500")], p = lag_order)
  fevd_result <- fevd(var_model, n.ahead = 10)  # Using a 10-day forecast horizon
  return(fevd_result)
}

estimate_VAR_FEVD_robust
# Create a function to calculate the 10th percentile and 90th percentile
calculate_percentiles <- function(fevd_results, percentile) {
  spillover_percentiles <- sapply(nifty, sp500, function(x) quantile(x, probs = c(percentile)))
  return(spillover_percentiles)
}

# Simulate results for different lag orders (for robustness)
set.seed(123)  # Set a seed for reproducibility
num_simulations <- 100  # Number of simulations
lag_orders <- sample(1:10, num_simulations, replace = TRUE)  # Randomly select lag orders

# Calculate percentiles for each simulation
percentile_10 <- calculate_percentiles(replicate(num_simulations, {
  fevd_result <- estimate_VAR_FEVD_robust(before_conflict_data, lag_orders[1])
  calculate_percentiles(fevd_result, 0.10)
}), 0.10)

percentile_90 <- calculate_percentiles(replicate(num_simulations, {
  fevd_result <- estimate_VAR_FEVD_robust(before_conflict_data, lag_orders[1])
  calculate_percentiles(fevd_result, 0.90)
}), 0.90)

# Create a plot showing the robustness of results
robustness_plot <- ggplot(data.frame(Lag_Order = lag_orders, Percentile_10 = percentile_10, Percentile_90 = percentile_90), aes(x = Lag_Order)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Percentile_10, ymax = Percentile_90), fill = "blue", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = rowMeans(cbind(Percentile_10, Percentile_90))), color = "blue") +
  labs(title = "Robustness of Results (VAR Lag Order Selection)",
       x = "Lag Order", y = "Percentile") +
  theme_minimal()

# Print the robustness plot
print(robustness_plot)

```
